title: Mandatory Dutch and invalidity of employment documents
summary: The decree of July 19, 1973 imposes Dutch for social relations and personnel documents within its territorial scope. A document contrary to the decree risks invalidity.
body: Articles 2 to 5 target employers having a place of business in the Dutch-speaking region. Verify the special regime of municipalities with facilities. Article 4, § 4, also covers relations with candidates before hiring, even if no contract is ultimately concluded.

Article 5 imposes a Dutch version. For certain workers exercising freedom of movement, an additional contractual version in an official EU or EEA language understood by the parties is admitted. In case of divergence, Dutch prevails. Section 5 allows testing other languages during selection.

According to Article 10, the judge finds invalidity ex officio and orders replacement of documents. Regularization only takes effect from the replacement according to the provided terms. Invalidity cannot harm the worker; the employer is liable for damage caused. The effective dates of the articles are indicated in the consolidated text.

title: Public job postings, internal postings, and interviews
summary: A public job posting by a private company is not automatically subject to Dutch. The official FAQ distinguishes public postings from internal documents and interviews.
body: The Flemish authority explicitly allows a commercial company to publish a job posting in another language in a newspaper. Therefore, the Language Decree should not be transformed into a general prohibition of public announcements in French or English.

A posting circulated internally to workers is a document intended for personnel and must respect the legally prescribed language. For a private company in a linguistically homogeneous municipality in Flanders, the interview is conducted in Dutch; another language can be used to test the candidate's language skills.

Public service job postings follow legislation on administrative languages. Verify the nature of the employer, the office concerned, and the public or internal nature of the distribution before choosing the language.

title: Equal treatment in Flemish competencies
summary: The decree of July 10, 2008 prohibits discrimination in matters falling under Flemish competencies, notably training and placement. The decree of May 8, 2002 must also be examined when it provides greater protection to the person.
body: Articles 15 and 15bis cover direct and indirect discrimination, harassment, instructions to discriminate, and refusal of reasonable accommodations. Protected criteria include notably age, sex, origin, disability, language, and family responsibilities.

Article 20, in its version applicable since June 7, 2026, targets in particular selection criteria, access to employment, vocational training, and placement, within the limits of the competencies of the Flemish Community and Region. Do not present this decree as replacing all federal labour legislation.

For situations subject to the decree, Article 26bis requires facilitating requests for reasonable accommodations and informing the applicant of follow-up within 30 days. An exceptional extension of 30 days must be justified and announced within the initial period.

title: Sectoral discrimination tests announced in 2026
summary: The program announced on July 29, 2026 measures discrimination in hiring related to origin and advanced age. These sectoral tests have an awareness-raising objective, without individual legal sanctions.
body: The public tender covers the 30 sectors participating in the tenth generation of sectoral agreements for 2026-2028. Depending on recruitment practices, researchers will use fictitious applications sent to real offers or fictitious phone calls.

The publication provides for aggregated results by sector; company names will not be published and individual results will remain confidential. To prepare for recruitment, apply consistent and explainable criteria to comparable candidates.

As of September 30, 2026, this source describes a program in preparation: contract award expected in autumn, then test implementation, with sectoral reports expected in spring 2028. It does not prove that tests have already begun.

title: End of Flemish reduction for low-skilled youth
summary: No new entitlement to this reduction opens for entry into service after June 30, 2024. The last transitional entitlements end in the first quarter of 2026 inclusive.
body: ONSS 2026/3 instructions concern workers employed in a Flemish establishment unit or dependent on it. The old reduction for low-skilled youth covered the quarter of hiring and the following seven, under conditions.

ONSS clarifies that code 6300 can no longer open an entitlement since the third quarter of 2024. An entitlement opened no later than the second quarter of 2024 could still be requested until the first quarter of 2026. For hiring on September 30, 2026, do not include this old reduction in the projected salary cost.

The reduction for alternating apprentices was already abolished on July 1, 2023 without transition. The disappearance of these reductions does not by itself eliminate federal obligations relating to youth employment.

title: End of Flemish reductions for older workers
summary: The reduction for already employed older workers is abolished as of July 1, 2025. The transition for former older job seekers hired before July 2024 ends in the first quarter of 2026.
body: ONSS instructions distinguish already employed older workers from recruited older job seekers. For the latter, entry into service after June 30, 2024 no longer opens an entitlement; previous entitlements could run during the hiring quarter and the following seven.

Code 6321 could still be requested for previous entitlements until the first quarter of 2026 inclusive. The reduction for already employed workers, code 6320, ended in the third quarter of 2025. The page retains an old reference to 2028, but the correction just before and the body of the instructions explicitly indicate the end in 2025.
For recruitment in September 2026 in a Flemish unit, do not promise any of these old age-related reductions. Regularizations of prior periods must be assessed according to the quarter concerned.

title: Publish a VDAB offer with current occupations and skills
summary: Since January 13, 2026, job posting entry on the employer portal uses Competent 2.0. The recruiter must select occupations and skills from this nomenclature.
body: A posting entered via werkgevers.vdab.be can no longer use Competent 1.0 data since January 13, 2026. Verify the selected occupation and proposed skills when creating or updating a posting.

For the Vacature Posting API, the source describes a transition whose end date is not yet indicated. It accepts one version or the other during this transition, but prohibits mixing them in the same offer: this combination results in rejection. Old data accepted are converted to Competent 2.0 for display.

title: IBO : convention, durée et engagement d’embauche
summary: IBO rules applicable since January 1, 2026 require a prior agreement and hiring after training. The arrangement also covers eligible Brussels establishments.
body: Articles 90 to 95 of the Decree of June 5, 2009 require an agreement signed by VDAB, the employer, and the trainee before the start. The candidate must be registered with VDAB; check restrictions concerning previous employment and resignation. The employer declares the IBO in Dimona before its start.

Article 97 sets a duration of 4 to 26 weeks, at least half-time and minimum 17.5 hours per week. The training plan must be approved. According to Article 93, bonus and travel expenses are paid no later than the seventh day of the following month.

Article 107 provides for a permanent contract starting the day after training; a fixed-term contract is allowed if the employer demonstrates to VDAB that it matches their usual hiring policy. The job must match the learned function, with at least the same schedule, and last at least as long as the IBO.

title: Single permit for a skilled occupation
summary: For a function on the migration list exercised for more than 90 days, the employer requests a single permit via Working in Belgium. Authorization for this category is limited to one year, even with a permanent contract.
body: Select the Migratielijst middengeschoolde functies category and gather proof of identity, residence, health insurance, and other required documents, along with a dated and signed contract. The list of required documents depends on the candidate's situation; submit a complete file at the single counter.

The regional service examines the work, then the Immigration Office examines the residence. A favorable decision on work alone does not yet constitute the single permit. Verify all authorizations and residence documents before starting work.

For this category, renew authorization annually even if the contract is permanent. The page requires filing the renewal at least two months and at most six months before expiration. A worker coming from abroad must register with the municipality within eight business days after arrival.

title: Flemish fee of 180 € for single permit
summary: Since September 1, 2026, a single permit application intended for Flanders entails a regional fee of €180. Payment must occur within 15 days of filing.
body: The amount of €180 applies to initial applications and renewals, in addition to the federal fee for residence. Work card applications are excluded. The regional amount is indexed each January 1; do not automatically reuse the 2026 amount for a later year.

After effectively submitting the file to the single counter, pay the request associated with the file number. If not paid within 15 days, the file is automatically closed. Processing begins only when the file is complete and payment is received and processed.
The paid fee is not refunded, including in case of refusal, withdrawal, or cancellation. Plan for payment and single counter access rights in the recruitment timeline, particularly for renewal.

title: Migration list of skilled occupations
summary: The list from the ministerial decree of December 1, 2025 opens a procedure without prior labour market testing. It is distinct from VDAB's general shortage occupation list.
body: Since January 1, 2026, verify the function and its tasks in the current migration list. The page mentions in particular roofers, excavating machine operators, and nursing assistants. A similarity in title is not sufficient: some descriptions expressly exclude similar activities.

Truck drivers are among the functions removed from this procedure. An existing authorization can be renewed for the same function with the same employer. A change of employer requires examining the Overige category if the occupation remains on the VDAB list.

The employer must apply the joint commission and classification corresponding to an experienced or qualified worker, never an unqualified classification for these functions. Posting and employment by a foreign company are not allowed in this category.

title: Economic migration: labour market test and posting for nine weeks
summary: Since January 1, 2026, the general route of Article 18 requires a VDAB shortage occupation, level 3 or 4 qualification, and prior publication. This route is distinct from categories with special rules.
body: Article 18, § 1, of the Decree of December 7, 2018 makes admissibility conditional on an offer published on VDAB and EURES platforms for at least nine consecutive weeks in the four months preceding the application. Also verify the occupation is listed on the VDAB list and the required qualification level.

The administration presumes that an appropriate candidate is available if the local tension indicator remains 12 or higher throughout this four-month period, if the offer requirements are disproportionate, or if the employer does not cooperate with VDAB. Document the search and cooperation with placement.

Section 2 provides a presumption of shortage for occupations on the ministerial list. Do not apply the nine-week test indiscriminately to all permit categories; first identify the legal route for recruitment.

title: VOP: only previous files subsist
summary: The Vlaamse ondersteuningspremie can no longer be requested for new hiring since July 1, 2023. Bonuses already awarded subsist during their award period; new requests fall under individueel maatwerk.
body: An employer benefiting no later than June 30, 2023 retains VOP for the awarded period. They check the decision and calculations in the WSE-loket. Since July 1, 2023, no extension or increase is granted within the VOP system.

For a five-year VOP, request evaluation in the individueel maatwerk system at least five months before its expiry. For a two-year VOP, the worker must have their support needs confirmed by VDAB before the employer submits the new request.

The service recalculates the bonus based on DmfA. Report changes of company, account, or contact; do not announce VOP as aid open for 2026 recruitment. This sheet describes a transitional system still applicable to existing files.

title: Disability: wage subsidy and individual support
summary: Individueel maatwerk supports employment of persons whose support needs are recognized by VDAB. Territorial conditions differ between the wage subsidy and support subsidy.
body: The decree of January 14, 2022, applicable for these provisions since July 1, 2023, targets notably persons residing in the Flemish Region, as well as those residing in another EU or EEA state and working in Flanders. Verify VDAB's indication before calculating aid.

Articles 15 and 20 distinguish the wage subsidy, which can notably cover employment on Belgian territory, from the support subsidy, reserved for an establishment in the Flemish Region. A filter based only on the Flemish workplace would therefore exclude certain wage subsidy beneficiaries.

Articles 12 and 16 provide, for workers with disabilities, a maximum duration of five years renewable after evaluation and a subsidy between 20% and 75% of the capped reference wage. For extremely vulnerable workers, the maximum duration is 24 months and the range 20% to 50%. The actual amount depends on the individual decision.

title: VDAB shortage occupations: 2026 edition
summary: The VDAB study published on February 1, 2026 identifies 227 shortage occupations. It helps adapt candidate searches and training opportunities to the occupation concerned.
body: The report distinguishes the lack of candidates, the gap between their skills and those sought, and working conditions that make the position less attractive. For a difficult-to-fill offer, examine the stated cause before raising diploma or experience requirements.

The list includes notably nurses, nursing assistants, accountants, developers, system administrators, payroll advisors, and truck drivers. Some entries are limited to specific contexts: for physiotherapists, the shortage targets salaried employment in elderly care.

VDAB changed its occupation structure in 2026: the total number is not directly comparable to previous years. The list describes recruitment difficulties and helps guide training; it does not exempt from verifying legal conditions for access to the profession.

title: Non-EU students: residence and weekly limit
summary: A foreign student with a valid residence title granting restricted labour market access can work without a separate authorization request, under conditions. During the school year, the limit is 20 hours per week.
body: The Flemish page targets foreign students studying in a Belgian establishment and holding a valid residence title. Check the electronic Card A and the arbeidsmarkt – beperkt mention, as well as its validity date, before organizing work.

Work must remain compatible with studies and not exceed 20 hours per week outside school holidays. The 20-hour limit does not apply during school holidays. A student contract offer alone is not sufficient to establish the right to work: keep verifying status and adapt hours to the period concerned.
